plain_text:
It's no secret that having shingles can be pretty miserable, but
getting vaccinated is an easy way to protect yourself
semantic_text: It's no secret that having shingles can be pretty miserable, but getting vaccinated is an easy way to protect yourself

plain_text:
hingles, also known as herpes zoster, is a painful, often
debilitating rash that affects roughly 1 million people
each year.
semantic_text: hingles, also known as herpes zoster, is a painful, often debilitating rash that affects roughly 1 million people each year.

plain_text:
Fortunately, the current shingles vaccine, known by the brand
name Shingrix, is highly effective at preventing shingles and its
side effects.
semantic_text: Fortunately, the current shingles vaccine, known by the brand name Shingrix, is highly effective at preventing shingles and its side effects.

plain_text:
Shingles is a painful rash or blisters on the skin. It is caused by
the same virus—herpes varicella zoster—that causes chickenpox,
which is highly contagious. Chickenpox usually affects kids under
age 15 and creates an itchy, uncomfortable rash that turns into
blisters. While shingles itself is not contagious, you can also catch
chickenpox from someone who has shingles if you have direct
contact with fluid from their rash.
semantic_text: Shingles is a painful rash or blisters on the skin. It is caused by the same virus—herpes varicella zoster—that causes chickenpox, which is highly contagious. Chickenpox usually affects kids under age 15 and creates an itchy, uncomfortable rash that turns into blisters. While shingles itself is not contagious, you can also catch chickenpox from someone who has shingles if you have direct contact with fluid from their rash.

plain_text:
About half of all shingles cases are
in adults ages 60 or older. The chance
of developing shingles becomes much
greater by age 70.
semantic_text: About half of all shingles cases are in adults ages 60 or older. The chance of developing shingles becomes much greater by age 70.

plain_text:
After a person recovers from chickenpox, the virus stays dormant
in certain nerve cells in the body and can reactivate later in life.
This second eruption of the chickenpox virus is called shingles.
semantic_text: After a person recovers from chickenpox, the virus stays dormant in certain nerve cells in the body and can reactivate later in life. This second eruption of the chickenpox virus is called shingles.

plain_text:
Shingles typically appears as a painful rash or blisters. It often
develops in a small area on one side of the body. It can also cause
burning, itching, tingling, and even numbness in the affected area.
Some people may also experience a fever, headache, chills, and an
upset stomach.
semantic_text: Shingles typically appears as a painful rash or blisters. It often develops in a small area on one side of the body. It can also cause burning, itching, tingling, and even numbness in the affected area. Some people may also experience a fever, headache, chills, and an upset stomach.

plain_text:
Anyone who has had chickenpox is at risk for shingles, especially
as they get older. You can't develop shingles unless you've been
exposed to the chickenpox virus. However, more than 99% of
Americans born in or before 1980 have had chickenpox, even if
they don't remember having it.
semantic_text: Anyone who has had chickenpox is at risk for shingles, especially as they get older. You can't develop shingles unless you've been exposed to the chickenpox virus. However, more than 99% of Americans born in or before 1980 have had chickenpox, even if they don't remember having it.

plain_text:
About 1 in 3 people in the United States will develop shingles in
their lifetime, usually after age 50. Although shingles can affect
younger adults and even children, it is most common in older adults.
People with weakened immune systems are also at greater risk.
semantic_text: About 1 in 3 people in the United States will develop shingles in their lifetime, usually after age 50. Although shingles can affect younger adults and even children, it is most common in older adults. People with weakened immune systems are also at greater risk.

plain_text:
While shingles itself can be very painful and uncomfortable, it can
also lead to serious complications. The most common complication
is postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), a condition that causes severe nerve
pain in the areas affected by the shingles rash. PHN pain can last for
weeks or even months after the rash clears up. For some people, the
pain is so severe that it hurts to put on clothing. Fortunately, it usually
gets better over time.
semantic_text: While shingles itself can be very painful and uncomfortable, it can also lead to serious complications. The most common complication is postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), a condition that causes severe nerve pain in the areas affected by the shingles rash. PHN pain can last for weeks or even months after the rash clears up. For some people, the pain is so severe that it hurts to put on clothing. Fortunately, it usually gets better over time.

plain_text:
Other potential complications include vision loss or hearing
problems if it develops near the eyes or ears. Very rarely, shingles
can also lead to pneumonia, brain inflammation, or even death.
semantic_text: Other potential complications include vision loss or hearing problems if it develops near the eyes or ears. Very rarely, shingles can also lead to pneumonia, brain inflammation, or even death.

plain_text:
Treating shingles quickly with antiviral drugs can shorten the duration
and reduce the severity of its symptoms. These medications include
acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir.
semantic_text: Treating shingles quickly with antiviral drugs can shorten the duration and reduce the severity of its symptoms. These medications include acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir.

plain_text:
For most healthy people who get treatment quickly, shingles
usually goes away within three to five weeks, and the blisters often
leave no scars. However, some people may experience lingering pain
from PHN.
semantic_text: For most healthy people who get treatment quickly, shingles usually goes away within three to five weeks, and the blisters often leave no scars. However, some people may experience lingering pain from PHN.
